paras: The killing of Isaac Hicks was the fatal shooting of a Black man by two Savannah policemen at a railway section camp outside Savannah, Georgia, in late December 1881, while they were searching for a different man. Hicks ran from a shanty when the officers came to the door, was shot in three places, and died the next morning at the police barracks. The Savannah Morning News headlined the case "The Wrong Man Killed," and under a coroner's jury's majority verdict the officers were held for the grand jury.

Earlier that Wednesday night, Elias Harris, described as colored, was shot near Eastern Hall by the yard of the Savannah, Florida and Western Railway, and John Lanier, also colored, was accused of the shooting and fled. Jackson Davis, a colored man who had been present, went to the police barracks and said he could lead an officer to where he believed Lanier was hiding. Lieutenant J. T. Howard sent Policemen John Crowley and W. F. Nungazer with Davis to arrest Lanier, and he testified afterward that the policemen had no warrants.

The party left shortly after ten o'clock for the junction of the White Bluff road and the railway, about a mile and a half from the city, where the road's section hands were quartered. There the section master, F. M. Murray, was asked whether there were "any strange negroes in his camp" and led the officers to one of the shanties. A man inside opened the door, shut it on seeing the officers, tried the window, and then broke out the door and ran.

The officers ordered him to stop, and when he kept running he was fired on several times, fell, rose, and fell again at another shot. When the party reached him, they found that he was not Lanier but Isaac Hicks. Hicks was carried by wagon to the barracks, arriving about 1:15 a.m., where Dr. J. T. McFarland found a gunshot wound in the left temple and judged it fatal; he died that morning.

The coroner's jury viewed the body and heard testimony at the court house. Davis testified that Hicks "resembled Lanier greatly," while Jack Williams, who had been lying beside Hicks, said the men outside threatened to shoot if he did not stop, that he heard three pistol shots, and that Hicks was "a quiet, peaceable man." In his statement Nungazer said he had called on the man to halt or be shot, and Howard, recalled, said the men he sent were "cool and collected."

The jury returned two verdicts, and under the majority verdict the officers were held to await the action of the grand jury. Harris died at the Georgia Infirmary the next day, and Lanier had not been caught; no report of grand jury action or a trial of the officers appears in the coverage.

The only coverage found is in the Savannah Morning News, on 30 and 31 December. Its first report, "A Double Tragedy," began with the morning report that a colored man had been killed in a row at a dance and his assailant shot by a policeman, then corrected it under the headline "The Wrong Man Killed." The paper printed the inquest testimony at length, including witnesses who contradicted the identification, and noted that the policeman's name should read W. F. Papot. Its follow-up the next day described Hicks as "an innocent man" killed in the pursuit of Lanier, without comment on the officers.

Accounts at the inquest differed on whether Hicks was identified aloud: the paper's narrative, Davis and Nungazer said Davis called out "that's the man," while Williams heard no such call and Murray said no call was made for "Lanier." The report's opening paragraph put the death at about eight o'clock, but Howard testified that Hicks died at six, and the follow-up dated the Harris shooting the 27th rather than simply "Wednesday night."

reader.title: Killing of Isaac Hicks
bases: Two city policemen sent to arrest a murder suspect shot and killed Isaac Hicks, a different man, as he ran from them; no crowd was involved (A1, A2).
All coverage comes from one paper, the Savannah Morning News, in a report and its continuation (A1, A2) and a next-day follow-up (A3); no other paper's report was found.

accounts.label: Newspaper narrative
accounts.gist: Davis called out 'that's the man,' the officers yelled to the fugitive to stop, and when he kept running he was fired on several times; he was then found to be Hicks, not Lanier.

accounts.label: Policeman Nungazer's statement
accounts.gist: The man shut the door, tried the window, then broke out and ran; Davis said 'That is the man,' and Nungazer called him to halt or be shot; the printed statement breaks off there.

accounts.label: Jack Williams (housemate)
accounts.gist: Hicks got up to open the door when Murray called, then ran; the men said they would shoot if he did not stop, and Williams heard three shots; he heard no one say 'that was the man' and called Hicks quiet and peaceable.

accounts.label: Section master Murray
accounts.gist: No call was made for 'Lanier' when the man ran out, and he could not say whether the fugitive could have been caught.

accounts.label: Coroner's jury
accounts.gist: Returned two verdicts; under the majority verdict the officers were held for the grand jury.

framing.detail: The Savannah Morning News headlined 'A Double Tragedy' and 'The Wrong Man Killed,' printed the inquest testimony of officers and Black witnesses alike, and the next day called Hicks 'an innocent man,' without editorial comment on the officers.

versions.value: Davis called out 'that's the man' as the man ran (narrative, Davis, Nungazer)
No one was heard to say 'that was the man' and no call was made for 'Lanier' (Williams, Murray)

conflicts.note: Both versions are inquest testimony printed in the same report.

versions.value: about eight o'clock in the morning (opening paragraph, reporting the rumor)
6 o'clock this morning (Lieut. Howard's sworn testimony)

conflicts.note: Howard's sworn testimony is the more direct source; the opening paragraph relays the morning report.
The Hicks shooting followed the same night, so the date of the event depends on which is right.

versions.value: W. F. Papot, 'the former surname being that under which he was born'

conflicts.note: The paper itself made the correction.
